title: Canonical unbounded right-derived adjunctions commute with canonical shifts
statement:
Let C and D be abelian categories with the recorded unbounded derived categories, and suppose D has K-injective resolutions. If L is an exact additive left adjoint to an additive R, then the canonical adjunction D(L) left adjoint to the K-injective right derived functor R(R) commutes with their fixed canonical shifts. The conclusion retains the existing K-injective shift, not an arbitrary transported shift.

theorem canonicalRightDerivedAdjunctionShift
    {C D : Type*} [Category C] [Category D] [Abelian C] [Abelian D]
    [HasDerivedCategory C] [HasDerivedCategory D] [HasKInjectiveResolutions D]
    {L : C ⥤ D} {R : D ⥤ C} [L.Additive] [R.Additive]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits L] [PreservesFiniteColimits L] (adj : L ⊣ R) :
    adj.mapDerivedCategoryRightDerivedAdjunction.CommShift ℤ

source.place: Tags 0DVC (pre-derived adjoint functors) and 0A8D (adjoint-is-exact), with sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A6 for unbounded derived adjunctions.

proof.text: Let E be the equivalence from K-injective homotopy objects to D(D). The inverse comparison R(R) to E inverse followed by termwise R and Qh is shift-compatible by construction. The defining formula expresses its components as the canonical right-derived unit followed by R(R) of E's counit. Naturality along E's unit and the triangle identity therefore identify the restriction of the canonical unit to K-injectives with a composite of shift-compatible transformations. Every homotopy object admits a quasi-isomorphism to such an object. NatTrans.CommShift.of_whiskerLeft gives shift compatibility of the entire canonical right-derived unit.

The homotopy adjunction unit commutes with shifts. The derived adjunction unit is normalized by its composite with R(R) of the exact L factorization: it is Qh of the homotopy unit followed by the canonical right-derived unit. Equality of transformations into D(L) followed by R(R) can be detected by the right Kan property of D(L), after taking the adjoint of postcomposition by R(R). Apply that detection to the two shift squares: their composites are equal by the normalized unit formula. This proves that the derived adjunction unit commutes with shifts. Adjunction.CommShift.mk' gives the counit compatibility by the triangle identities.
